feedback: Written before this candidate races. Iteration 1 (±0.06 m span, y=0.03 m, 16 mm footprints) gave zero line losses but max_error of 0.0610 to 0.0613 m on all tracks, the lowest error seen. Iteration 2 (same geometry, row moved to y=0.05 m, ki 0.3) raised oval max_error to 0.0637 m and gave one slalom line loss per run, so the forward row is rejected as the lever. Iteration 0 (±0.04 m span, 12 mm footprints) lost the tape near 0.05 m. I am passing your span test to the Integrator's controller: the row returns to y=0.03 m and the span widens to ±0.08 m. What I had to change in the controller: weights are rescaled to 25 per metre (the weights are the same numbers as before), and kp is raised to 8.0 to keep the effective gain. The bias remains unexplained. Next race guidance: if line_loss_events stays at zero on the slalom and s-bend and max_error is near 0.061 m on the oval, the remaining limit is controller bias, so keep the geometry fixed. If line losses persist at ±0.08 m, change the footprint to 0.012 m or move the row back, not forward. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the wider span, reduce mass to 0.5 kg.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is still 1 or more on the slalom or s-bend at sensor span ±0.08 m, reduce sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m with the same seven positions, because the iteration 0 12 mm footprints gave a clean graded signal and the 16 mm footprint has been the only geometry change since then.

If line losses are zero but max_error stays above 0.06 m on the oval, keep the geometry fixed and move the row back to y = 0.01 m (not forward), since the forward row in iteration 2 raised max_error from 0.0613 to 0.0637 m.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the ±0.08 m span, reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg to cut yaw inertia, keeping the sensor geometry fixed.
